newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products -- Gulf gasoline diffs firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products -- Gulf gasoline diffs firm.

text.p: U.S. Gulf gasoline differentials firmed slightly on Tuesday in a continuation of yesterday's surge although the Midcontinent slid amid a lack of buying interest, players said.
NYMEX futures were also down as a price consolidation was accelerated by news Iraq was to submit its oil pricing formula in the next few hours.
NYMEX gasoline was off 0.54 cents at 66.20 cents a gallon and heating was down 0.54 cent at 57.90 cents and crude was down 10 cents at $20.65 a barrel.

U.S. Gulf unleaded gasoline and heating oil differentials firmed in light activity continuing Monday's surge as buyers bid up prompt barrels. The firming is one day before the scheduling deadline for M1-grade front 23rd cycle of conventional unleaded gasoline.
Players said 2.30 cents over the scrren for prompt M1 was done this morning, putting the range at 2.25/2.40 cents. Any months rose a quarter cent to 2.25/2.50 cents below the screen.
Prompt A1 reformulated southern-grade unleaded also firmed, about a quarter cent to 5.25/5.50 cents.
Prompt two oil for the back 22d cycle firmed about 0.10 cent to 2.40/2.25 cents below the September screen amid some refiner demand.

Traders said they were expecting more refiner interest in the spot distillate market. "It's cheaper for cat crackers to use distillate than to buy gasoline so its shortening up on the two oil supply," said a U.S. trader.
Gasoline differentials remained strong in early Tuesday action, according to market players, with prompt barrels remaining in high demand.
Prompt reformulated A2 gasoline differentials firmed modestly, with offers rising about 0.25 cent to sit at 7.50 cents a gallon over the September NYMEX.

Tightness in the MTBE market due to some recent supply problems forced prices of the gasoline additive sharply higher in recent weeks. Prices for MTBE have weakened modestly in the past few days, though they still remain at fairly high levels.
Prompt regular conventional M2 gasoline differentials hovered between 2.50 and 2.75 cents over the nearby NYMEX contract, about unchanged from late Monday levels, according to traders.

Premium 93-octane reformulated D2 gasoline for prompt delivery changed hands at 14.5 cents over the September futures, while barrels for delivery near mid-month were talked at about 12.00 cents over the futures.

Midcontinent unleaded gasoline markets continued slide due to a lack of buyers. Group Three unleaded was down to 4.50/4.75 cents, losing 1.25 cents from late Monday. Any months wer pegged 1.75/2.00 cents.
Chicago unleaded also fell 1.25 cents to 4.50/4.75 cents with the any months at 2.25/2.50 cents.
